newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AUSTRALIAN BONDS VULNERABLE ON U.S. WORRIES.
newsitem.headline: AUSTRALIAN BONDS VULNERABLE ON U.S. WORRIES.

text.p: *Long-dated Australian bonds looked vulnerable going into the weekend with futures hovering just above key support, and will be highly dependent on the U.S. for the next move.
*RBA governor speech only highlight seen next week.
Long dated Australian bonds looked vulnerable going into the weekend and were hovering only just above key support after a sharp U.S.-led sell-off.
U.S. Treasuries have been under pressure all week since last Friday's strong employment and NAPM data, and this week's quarterly refunding auctions have only just made expectations.

Local traders said that while the Australian market has shown some resilience to the U.S. slide on a fundamental basis, technicals are also beginning to sour in anticipation of further selling pressure in the U.S. later on Friday.

The long end attracted heavy liquidation after the September 10-year bond futures contract slid through suupport at 93.470 and was looking fragile at just above 93.400, which technical analysts said the market needs to hold to keep the recent upward trend intact.

The U.S. market is also likely to dominate domestic activity next as local major data is fairly thin, although a speech by Reserve Bank governor Ian Macfarlane in Perth on Tuesday may provide some clues for the outlook to future monetary policy.
Meanwhile, the U.S. faces a raft of key indicators including CPI, PPI and retail sales.

The local market's weak tone saw it underperform against both U.S. and Canadian debt, although the negative spread against New Zealand continued to widen as the N.Z. dollar slid again to a new 29 month low against the U.S.
